full_judgment: 8. From the provisions of clause (g) it appears that for merely taking a loan, a loanee cannot be said to be disqualified. In the agreement itself or in any other papers some time limit must be given to repay the loan and if the loanee fails to fulfill the terms of the contract and fails to repay the loan within the stipulated time, he may be called a defaulter. There is no averment in the plaint of the suit (Annexure-D) as to the terms and conditions under which the loan was taken. Nothing has been said as to whether there has been any violation of any terms regarding the time limit or whether there was at all any time limit. Loan was taken on 12.9.85 and the suit was filed on 14.5.87 i.e. within less than 2 years time from taking of the loan. There are various kinds of loan that one may take from a bank. Some loans may be simply overdraft facilities, for which the bank may not fix anytime limit. The bank usually makes a demand for payment and when the loanee fails to repay the loan, the bank files a suit to save limitation. In order to attract the mischief of clause (g), it must be shown that the loan was to be repaid within a time-limit allowed by the bank. If the loan does not answer that description or if there is no evidence of the kind of loan granted by the bank, the mischief of clause (g) is not attracted. Since there is no assertion in the plaint as regards the time limit of repaying the loan, it has not been proved at all that the respondent No. 1 has taken from the bank any loan which answers the description of clause (g). The question of his being a defaulter docs not arise.
